why: The new examples made the model more willing to split off short sentence‑initial adverbial/participial leads and to cut adjacent to verbs/short complements; that produced some large gains where an initial adjunct or verb‑adjacent cut is helpful but caused more aggressive early cuts in short/mid pieces that broke up compound nouns and names, so overall H_set fell slightly (worse in the ≤5 bin).
lesson: Keep examples that permit verb‑adjacent and sentence‑initial adjunct cuts only when the remainder is clearly long or syntactically self‑contained, because otherwise the model will over‑apply those patterns and split short noun compounds and proper names.
